newsitem.title: UK: Novartis says Femara unique on tumours.
newsitem.headline: Novartis says Femara unique on tumours.

text.p: Life sciences group Novartis AG said on Monday its new hormone treatment for advanced breast cancer showed "unique" action against tumours.
Femara, which inhibits female hormones, had a measurably stronger effect on tumours and for longer in phase III clinical trials, researchers told a cancer conference in Vienna.

Tests showed another hormone treatment, megestrol acetate, caused either complete remission or shrinkage of the tumour in 16.4 percent of patients, as compared with 23.6 percent given Femara (letrozole), Novartis said in a statement released in London.

They conducted tests on how long the effects lasted. When Femara caused either complete remission or partial remission, or a stabilisation of condition, it lasted on average 707 days as compared with 374 days for aminoglutethimide, one of the other available hormone treatments.
Femara inhibits aromatase, which is the key enzyme for synthesising the female hormone oestrogen. It does not affect other hormones.
Used in advanced breast cancer, it can extend survival in women who have stopped responding to the standard drug tamoxifen, Novartis said. Zeneca plc is the main manufactuer of tamoxifen.
"Femara offers a unique combination of benefits of superior anti-tumour efficacy, superior tolerability and improved survival," the Novartis statement said. _-- London Newsroom +44 171 542 8958
